title: Inside an animal cell: what each part does
examples: What are the parts of an animal cell?

parts.label: Cell membrane
parts.note: Thin skin that controls what gets in
parts.ask: What does the cell membrane do?

explain.say: Imagine shrinking smaller than a speck of dust and floating inside your own cheek. You would be inside a cell, and you are built from about 30 trillion of them! Let's look around one together.

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: an animal cell. Look at the cell membrane, the cytoplasm and the nucleus. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: Inside an animal cell: what each part does

explain.say: See the big purple blob near the middle? That is the nucleus, the control room. It holds DNA, which is the set of instructions for running the cell. What do you think a cell would do without its instructions?

parts.label: Cell membrane
parts.note: Thin skin that controls what gets in
parts.ask: What does the cell membrane do?

explain.say: Now follow the thin edge all the way round. That is the cell membrane, a soft skin that lets food and oxygen in and waste out, like a guard at a gate. What should that guard let in, do you think?

parts.label: Cell membrane
parts.note: Thin skin that controls what gets in
parts.ask: What does the cell membrane do?

explain.say: Spot the little orange shapes with wiggly lines? Those are mitochondria. They release energy from sugar and oxygen, which is called respiration. Muscle cells are packed with them. Can you guess why?

parts.label: Cell membrane
parts.note: Thin skin that controls what gets in
parts.ask: What does the cell membrane do?

explain.say: Last, the tiny grey dots are ribosomes, which build proteins, the stuff your body is made from. Everything floats in cytoplasm, a watery jelly. Brilliant work! Wow fact: each nucleus holds about 2 metres of DNA, folded up.

faq.a: The nucleus holds DNA, the instructions for making proteins and running the cell. It controls what the cell does and copies its DNA when the cell divides.
asks: What is the control centre of a cell?

faq.q: What does the cell membrane do?
faq.a: The cell membrane is a thin, bendy layer around the cell. It controls what goes in and out, letting in glucose and oxygen and letting out carbon dioxide and waste.
asks: Tell me about the cell membrane

faq.a: Mitochondria are where aerobic respiration happens. They use glucose and oxygen to release energy that the cell can use for moving, growing and repairing.
asks: Why are mitochondria called the powerhouse?

faq.a: Ribosomes are tiny structures that join amino acids together to make proteins, following instructions copied from DNA. One cell can have millions of them.
asks: What makes proteins in a cell?

faq.q: How big is an animal cell?
faq.a: Most animal cells are about 10 to 30 micrometres across. A micrometre is a thousandth of a millimetre, so you need a microscope to see them.
asks: Can you see a cell without a microscope?

facts: An adult human body contains roughly 30 trillion human cells.
Animal cells have no cell wall, so they can take many different shapes.
Aerobic respiration takes place mainly inside mitochondria.

quiz.say: Which part of an animal cell controls what goes in and out?
quiz.show: Which part of an animal cell controls what goes in and out?
quiz.why: The cell membrane surrounds the cell and lets some substances through while keeping others out.

wrong.0: The nucleus holds DNA and controls the cell's activities, but it is not the gatekeeper.
wrong.2: Ribosomes build proteins; they do not control what enters the cell.

quiz.say: Where is most energy released from glucose in a cell?
quiz.show: Where is most energy released from glucose in a cell?
quiz.why: Aerobic respiration, which releases most of the energy from glucose, happens in the mitochondria.

wrong.1: The nucleus stores DNA; respiration does not happen there.
wrong.2: The membrane controls entry and exit but does not release energy from glucose.
